positions.name: MeridianGateMandate
positions.frame: By what authority is the Meridian deployment gate imposed — a declared precondition spanning requirement, scope, and ownership, rather than a negotiated or explained process?
positions.why: Across prose directive and fielded-label restatement alike, the speaker performs authority-ranking through mandatory-precondition language rather than persuasion: src-1's 'now requires… before it ships' and src-3's '**Gate**: … required' state the same rule in two registers (prose vs. technical label), src-4 extends that mandate's reach ('applies to staging and production'), and src-5 closes the loop by self-designating as the position-holder who owns and can enforce it ('**Owner**: Quinton Fairweather'). The power and relational reads mark all four as legitimate/authority-ranking acts — a gate set by declaration, not by consultation — and the style read notes src-3–src-5 share a bolded-label formula while src-1 states the identical rule in plain directive prose, which is why it belongs in the same read rather than a separate one. src-2 sits outside this frame: it supplies the causal justification (rational-persuasion/informational, market-pricing) rather than performing the mandate itself, so it does not join this group.
